title: Derived pullback commutes with derived tensor product on the constructible categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the coefficient categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with the finite bounded constructible category of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the derived-complete integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and arbitrary $M,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
 \mu_{f;M,N}:Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*N
$$
in the ambient derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$. In particular this applies to $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$, without asserting that their derived tensor product is bounded.

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ and $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, the same formula is an isomorphism in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$; the integral tensor product is the completed derived tensor product specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At finite level $\mu$ is the canonical tensor comparison for the morphism of ringed topoi induced by $f$. At integral level it is the functorial derived inverse limit of the finite comparisons on $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and $N_n=N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, using the canonical reduction identifications for completed pullback and tensor. At rational level it is the image of the integral comparison; at the $\Qlb$ level it is represented by the rational comparison over any common finite coefficient field, composed with the scalar-extension comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

These isomorphisms are natural in $M,N$, compatible with associativity, the signed commutativity and the unit isomorphisms of derived tensor, and compatible with composition: for $h:Z\to X$, $\mu_{f\circ h;M,N}$ is $\mu_{h;Lf^*M,Lf^*N}\circ Lh^*(\mu_{f;M,N})$ under the canonical composition identifications of pullbacks. They commute with finite reduction (including the derived change of coefficients $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$ for $m\geq n$) and with scalar extension through finite coefficient field extensions and into $\Qlb$.

Apply common-stage comparison naturality to the rational naturality just proved. NatIso.ofComponents packages the canonical common-stage components, with their specified values unchanged.

The finite comparison is already a natural isomorphism by finitePullbackTensorConstructionIso; its components are definitionally canonicalFinitePullbackTensor. Use the existing finite associativity, unit, composition and signed-braiding theorems. Use the recorded quotient, integral/rational scalar, rationalization-component, and whole-system evaluation equations. The actual integral reduction square is the existing counit calculation in the constraints module.

Supply the three higher composition equations from pullbackTensorCompositionCoherence, and the three unit statements from pullbackTensorUnitCoherence. These are the remaining separate structural diagrams of the original quotient-realization and coefficient-descent argument, not a renamed form of the whole comparison theorem. Assemble these clauses with the preceding natural isomorphisms, reduction equations, and all three associativity and braiding equations into the unchanged 26-fold conjunction.

The item's statement, stmt_deps and Lean records are unchanged.

Re-split check: every old step maps to a new node or to a reused existing node. Steps 1-3 go to finite-derived-comparison-normalization, 4-5 and 7-10 to completed-comparison-quotient-realization, and 11-12 to bilinear-comparison-coefficient-descent. Old step 6 stays as elementary assembly step 3 and cites lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible (1)+(2). The three nodes are of comparable size and none restates the parent: the finite node is for arbitrary ringed topoi with a coefficient square, the completed node is the representative-level realization, and the descent node is a generic statement for separately linear bifunctors. None duplicates an existing node: the cochain and limit/coherence/scalar-tower lemmas are pieces only, and the unary localization and common-stage descent nodes are unary or Perf-valued.

I tested the statements on small cases. Z/ℓ² on a point gives an unbounded derived tensor; f=id, E=L and zero inputs give identities; for ramified L/E, ϖ_E^n lies in ϖ_L^{en}, so the quotient maps exist without flatness. A torsion Hom tensored with E is 0. I checked the arrow types of the compositor equation, the coefficient square, the whole-system counit equation and the scalar square.

Three repairs are in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity:
(1) Step 5 did not say where the descent node's λ^U, λ^V and their identity and tower equations come from. They are F̂(α_T)α_F and (α_F⊗α_F)α_T of lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, and step 5 now cites it.
(2) Step 6 dropped old step 12's link to the common-stage category and the Q̄ operations. The descent node's induced V is (K, Lf_K^*A_K⊗Lf_K^*B_K), but the item's target is (Lf^*A)_K⊗(Lf^*B)_K; the two agree only through the θ^{f^*} classes. Step 6 now makes this identification and cites def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom and the scalar lemma.
(3) The completed node said its structural diagrams 'are diagrams' of strict systems without saying they commute. It now states that they are commuting diagrams whose limit images are the commuting diagrams of γ_E. This is true by its stmt_dep lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence.
